q2.title: Why build this, and why now?
q2.body:
- What problem does it solve, and what evidence shows it is real (tickets, data, requests)?
- What happens if we do nothing, or do it next quarter?
- Is this the root problem, or a symptom of something cheaper to fix?

q3.title: Who uses it, and who has a stake in it?
q3.body:
- Which user segments or roles are affected, and how many?
- Who owns the decision, who reviews it, who supports it after launch?
- Which other teams or services depend on the parts we touch?

q4.title: What is in scope, and what is explicitly out?
q4.body:
- List the smallest version that delivers the outcome; everything else is out or later.
- Which edge cases, platforms, locales or plans are excluded on purpose?
- What existing behavior must not change?

q5.title: What does success look like, and how is it measured?
q5.body:
- Propose 1-3 measurable metrics with a baseline and target.
- How and where is each metric collected, and when is it reviewed?
- What result would make us roll back or abandon the feature?

q6.title: How should we build it?
q6.body:
- Compare at least two approaches, including build vs. buy/reuse an existing library or service.
- Which existing patterns in the codebase does each approach follow or break?
- Rough effort, maintenance cost, and reversibility of each.

q7.title: What data model and API changes are needed?
q7.body:
- New or changed tables, fields, events, config; are any migrations destructive?
- New or changed endpoints, payloads, or public interfaces; are they backwards compatible?
- Who else consumes these contracts, and how are they versioned?

q8.title: Where does it live in the codebase and architecture?
q8.body:
- Which modules, services, or packages change; which new ones (if any) are created?
- Which layer owns the logic (UI, API, worker, database), and why there?
- Does it add coupling between components that are currently independent?

q9.title: How does it reach users, and in what order?
q9.body:
- Sequence the work so each step is shippable and reviewable on its own.
- What must be migrated or backfilled, and can it run before the code ships?
- How is it rolled back if something goes wrong after release?

q12.title: How will we test it?
q12.body:
- Which unit, integration, and end-to-end tests prove the success criteria?
- Which existing tests cover the code we change, and which gaps must be filled first?
- What needs manual or staged verification (UI, real integrations, load)?

q13.title: What are the security, privacy, and failure risks?
q13.body:
- Does it touch auth, permissions, secrets, or personal data; what is the threat model?
- What happens on partial failure, timeouts, retries, or bad input?
- Performance or cost impact at current and 10x scale?

o14.title: Add mode-declared node types
pros: Gives repo terms real kinds, validation and UI labels
cons: Requires coordinated config, template and viewer support
o14.rationale: The requested vocabulary needs a real word type, while scoped declarations avoid unrelated global types.

history.to: The requested vocabulary needs a real word type, while scoped declarations avoid unrelated global types.

o15.title: Keep using notes
cons: Words remain untyped and hard to validate or browse

q16.title: How should declarations stay maintainable?
q16.body: Prefer existing registries and data-driven config over one-off core conditions.

o17.title: Reuse keyed config sections
pros: Fits established inheritance and diff behavior
cons: Requires extending the shared section parser

o19.title: Serve mode authors, maintainers, agents and contributors
pros: One shared vocabulary supports humans and agents
cons: Requires clear human acceptance of new terms
o19.rationale: The request explicitly targets both humans and agents and makes human acceptance part of glossary building.

history.to: The request explicitly targets both humans and agents and makes human acceptance part of glossary building.

o20.title: Serve human maintainers only
cons: Agents and contributors may use inconsistent terms

q21.title: Who accepts new terms?
q21.body: New terms should start pending so a human can accept or reject them.

o24.title: Declare node types per mode scope
pros: Sub-tree types stay local and built-ins remain universal
cons: Scope validation must cover adds, moves and templates
o24.rationale: The brief requires scope-local types and rejects words outside their declaring sub-tree.

history.to: The brief requires scope-local types and rejects words outside their declaring sub-tree.

o25.title: Make every declared type global
cons: Leaks sub-mode vocabulary across the tree

q26.title: How should scoped declarations inherit?
q26.body: Keep inheritance predictable for child modes.

o28.title: Replace the entire section
pros: Easy to reason about in isolation

o29.title: Gate success on tests, package and viewer smoke
pros: Reproducible acceptance covers compatibility and published files
cons: Requires focused automated and headless checks
o29.rationale: The owner specified npm tests, lint, pack inclusion, CLI behavior and a headless viewer label/no-null check.

history.to: The owner specified npm tests, lint, pack inclusion, CLI behavior and a headless viewer label/no-null check.

o30.title: Wait for post-release adoption metrics
cons: Cannot validate the requested behavior before shipping

q31.title: What should block release?
q31.body: Use the checks specified in the implementation brief.

o34.title: Extend the existing config registries
pros: Small data-driven surface reuses established patterns
o34.rationale: SECTIONS, policy helpers and existing template paths provide the smallest extensible design without runtime dependencies.

history.to: SECTIONS, policy helpers and existing template paths provide the smallest extensible design without runtime dependencies.

q36.title: Where should type validation live?
q36.body: Keep each rule in its existing responsibility layer.

o37.title: Shared policy helpers
pros: Reusable by add, update, conform and templates

o39.title: Use keyed node_types config entries
pros: Supports merge, null removal, diff and scope
cons: Adds one section to config parsing
o39.rationale: A keyed section with required name, optional prefix/description and replaceable kinds matches existing config behavior.

history.to: A keyed section with required name, optional prefix/description and replaceable kinds matches existing config behavior.

o40.title: Use a separate global registry
cons: Breaks mode inheritance and scope semantics

q41.title: How should child modes override declarations?
q41.body: Preserve only the entry and list semantics requested.

o44.title: Extend existing backend and viewer modules
pros: Core, templates, config output and viewer remain aligned
o44.rationale: The change belongs in the existing config registry, policy, template schema/export and viewer editor.

history.to: The change belongs in the existing config registry, policy, template schema/export and viewer editor.

q46.title: Which viewer surfaces need the new type?
q46.body: Mirror scoped config helpers across viewer paths.

o47.title: Labels, colors, forms and mode editor

o49.title: Run unit, CLI, packaging and headless checks
pros: Covers config semantics, end-to-end usage and viewer output
cons: Headless checks are narrower than full interactive browser tests
o49.rationale: The requested tests cover legacy configs, scoping, templates, export, CLI and a headless snapshot.

history.to: The requested tests cover legacy configs, scoping, templates, export, CLI and a headless snapshot.

q51.title: What viewer evidence is sufficient?
q51.body: Use a fresh scratch app with the vocabulary mode.

o52.title: Headless screenshot and DOM assertions
pros: Fast, repeatable and checks the requested label

o53.title: Full browser interaction matrix
cons: Playwright is unavailable and would add upkeep

o54.title: Keep legacy configs safe and reject scope leaks
pros: Missing node_types defaults to empty and conform catches moved words
cons: Requires defensive reads in server and viewer
o54.rationale: Explicit missing-key helpers and scope conflict checks address the stated 0.4.x compatibility risk.

history.to: Explicit missing-key helpers and scope conflict checks address the stated 0.4.x compatibility risk.

o55.title: Assume every stored config is current

q56.title: How should malformed declarations fail?
q56.body: Reject invalid IDs, prefixes and duplicate kinds during config parsing.

o57.title: Validate early with clear paths
pros: Prevents malformed modes from being saved

q59.title: What is the rollback path?
q59.body: If the change causes regressions, revert the feature branch before the next package release.

o60.title: Revert before release
cons: Requires a new package release if already published
